# surtgis_algorithms::landscape - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/landscape/index.html

## Expand description

Landscape ecology algorithms

Moving-window landscape metrics for categorical raster data:

- **Shannon Diversity**: Information entropy index
- **Simpson Diversity**: Probability of interspecific encounter
- **Patch Density**: Number of distinct patches per unit area

Global landscape metrics (scalar output per patch/class/landscape):

- **Connected Components**: Label contiguous patches (Union-Find)
- **Patch Metrics**: PARA, FRAC, area, perimeter per patch
- **Class Metrics**: AI, COHESION per class
- **Landscape Metrics**: SHDI, SIDI global

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use connected_components::`- [Connectivity](https://docs.rs/connected_components/enum.Connectivity.html);

- `pub use patch_metrics::`- [PatchStats](https://docs.rs/patch_metrics/struct.PatchStats.html);
- `pub use patch_metrics::`- [patch_metrics](https://docs.rs/patch_metrics/fn.patch_metrics.html);
- `pub use patch_metrics::`- [patches_to_csv](https://docs.rs/patch_metrics/fn.patches_to_csv.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

# surtgis_algorithms::morphology - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/morphology/index.html

## Expand description

Mathematical morphology algorithms for raster processing

Classical morphological operations for image analysis:

- **Erosion**: minimum filter (shrinks bright regions)
- **Dilation**: maximum filter (expands bright regions)
- **Opening**: erosion then dilation (removes small bright features)
- **Closing**: dilation then erosion (fills small dark gaps)
- **Gradient**: dilation minus erosion (edge detection)
- **Top-hat**: original minus opening (bright feature extraction)
- **Black-hat**: closing minus original (dark feature extraction)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Black](https://docs.rs/struct.BlackHat.html)- Hat
- Black-hat algorithm
- [Black](https://docs.rs/struct.BlackHatParams.html)- HatParams
- Parameters for black-hat transform
- [Closing](https://docs.rs/struct.Closing.html)
- Closing algorithm
- [Closing](https://docs.rs/struct.ClosingParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for morphological closing
- [Dilate](https://docs.rs/struct.Dilate.html)
- Dilation algorithm
- [Dilate](https://docs.rs/struct.DilateParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for morphological dilation
- [Erode](https://docs.rs/struct.Erode.html)
- Erosion algorithm
- [Erode](https://docs.rs/struct.ErodeParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for morphological erosion
- [Gradient](https://docs.rs/struct.Gradient.html)
- Morphological gradient algorithm
- [Gradient](https://docs.rs/struct.GradientParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for morphological gradient
- [Opening](https://docs.rs/struct.Opening.html)
- Opening algorithm
- [Opening](https://docs.rs/struct.OpeningParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for morphological opening
- [TopHat](https://docs.rs/struct.TopHat.html)
- Top-hat (white top-hat) algorithm
- [TopHat](https://docs.rs/struct.TopHatParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for top-hat transform

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

# surtgis_algorithms::pansharpening - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/pansharpening/index.html

## Expand description

Pansharpening: fuse a high-resolution panchromatic image with a lower-resolution multispectral image to produce a high-resolution multispectral output.

All algorithms here expect the multispectral bands **already
upsampled** to pan resolution. The caller is responsible for the
upsampling step (use `vector::resample` or any GIS-standard
bilinear/cubic upsampler upstream).

Common contract: each function takes `pan: &Raster<f64>` and
`ms: &[&Raster<f64>]` (each MS band at pan resolution), and
returns `Vec<Raster<f64>>` — one sharpened band per input MS
band, in the same order.

Algorithms:

- **Brovey**(Gillespie et al. 1987) — simplest, fastest; per-band ratio against a synthetic pan from MS. Can saturate colours.
- **PCA**(Chavez et al. 1991) — replaces the first principal component of MS with histogram-matched pan. Works for arbitrary band count. Reuses the Jacobi eigensolver from- `classification::pca`.
- **Gram-Schmidt**(Laben & Brower 2000, US patent 6,011,875, expired 2018) — Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation of MS against a synthetic low-res pan, replace the first GS component with real pan, invert.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [brovey](https://docs.rs/fn.brovey.html)
- Apply the Brovey transform.
- [gram_](https://docs.rs/fn.gram_schmidt.html)- schmidt
- Apply Gram-Schmidt pansharpening (Laben & Brower 2000).
- [pca_](https://docs.rs/fn.pca_pansharpen.html)- pansharpen
- PCA pansharpening. NaN cells in any input are excluded from the covariance / statistics computation and emitted as NaN in every output band.

---

# surtgis_algorithms::sampling - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/sampling/index.html

## Expand description

Raster sampling primitives: point extraction, CNN patches, and polygon grid sampling.

These are the library-level building blocks behind the
`surtgis extract` and `surtgis extract-patches` CLI commands,
exposed so sibling crates can sample rasters without shelling out:

- `sample_at_points`
- `extract_patches`- `[n, bands, size, size]`f32 tensor.
- `grid_points_in_polygon`

All functions take world coordinates in the reference raster’s CRS and validate that the input rasters share one grid.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Patch](https://docs.rs/struct.PatchParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for `extract_patches`
- [Patches](https://docs.rs/struct.Patches.html)
- CNN-ready patch tensor produced by `extract_patches`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [extract_](https://docs.rs/fn.extract_patches.html)- patches
- Extract fixed-size multi-band patches centred on world-coordinate points.
- [grid_](https://docs.rs/fn.grid_points_in_polygon.html)- points_ - in_ - polygon
- Regular grid of cell-centre world coordinates inside a polygon.
- [sample_](https://docs.rs/fn.sample_at_points.html)- at_ - points
- Sample every raster at each world-coordinate point.

---

# surtgis_algorithms::segmentation - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/segmentation/index.html

## Expand description

Image segmentation algorithms.

- **SLIC**superpixels (Achanta et al. 2012). K-means in (n_bands + 2)-dimensional space with spatial-vs-spectral trade-off controlled by a compactness parameter.
- **Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher**graph segmentation (Felzenszwalb & Huttenlocher 2004). Region-merging on an 8-connected pixel graph with an adaptive threshold.

Both algorithms return a label raster (`Raster<i32>`), one
integer label per pixel, ready for downstream zonal statistics
(`statistics::zonal_statistics`) or patch metrics.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Felzenszwalb](https://docs.rs/struct.FelzenszwalbParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher graph-based segmentation.
- [Slic](https://docs.rs/struct.SlicParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for SLIC superpixel segmentation.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [felzenszwalb](https://docs.rs/fn.felzenszwalb.html)
- Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher segmentation.
- [slic](https://docs.rs/fn.slic.html)
- Compute SLIC superpixels from one or more bands.

---

# surtgis_algorithms::temporal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/temporal/index.html

## Expand description

Multi-temporal analysis algorithms

Per-pixel time-series analysis for satellite imagery:

- **Statistics**: mean, std, min, max, count, percentiles across time
- **Trend**: linear regression, Mann-Kendall, Sen’s slope
- **Anomaly**: z-score deviation from a reference period
- **Phenology**: vegetation phenology metrics (SOS, EOS, peak, amplitude)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Linear](https://docs.rs/struct.LinearTrendResult.html)- Trend - Result
- Result of per-pixel linear trend analysis.
- [Mann](https://docs.rs/struct.MannKendallResult.html)- Kendall - Result
- Result of Mann-Kendall trend test.
- [Phenology](https://docs.rs/struct.PhenologyParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for phenology extraction.
- [Phenology](https://docs.rs/struct.PhenologyResult.html)- Result
- Phenology result with multiple metric rasters.
- [Temporal](https://docs.rs/struct.TemporalStats.html)- Stats
- All temporal statistics in a single pass.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Anomaly](https://docs.rs/enum.AnomalyMethod.html)- Method
- Method for computing anomaly values.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [linear_](https://docs.rs/fn.linear_trend.html)- trend
- Per-pixel ordinary least squares linear regression.
- [mann_](https://docs.rs/fn.mann_kendall.html)- kendall
- Mann-Kendall non-parametric trend test with Sen’s slope.
- [sens_](https://docs.rs/fn.sens_slope.html)- slope
- Per-pixel Sen’s slope estimator (standalone, without full Mann-Kendall test).
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_anomaly.html)- anomaly
- Compute temporal anomaly: how each target raster deviates from a reference period.
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_count.html)- count
- Per-pixel count of valid (non-NaN) observations across time.
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_max.html)- max
- Per-pixel maximum across time.
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_mean.html)- mean
- Per-pixel mean across time.
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_min.html)- min
- Per-pixel minimum across time.
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_percentile.html)- percentile
- Per-pixel percentile (0-100) across time.
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_stats.html)- stats
- Compute all temporal statistics in a single pass (more efficient than calling each separately).
- [temporal_](https://docs.rs/fn.temporal_std.html)- std
- Per-pixel standard deviation across time.
- [vegetation_](https://docs.rs/fn.vegetation_phenology.html)- phenology
- Extract vegetation phenology metrics from an NDVI/EVI time series.

# surtgis_algorithms::terrain - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/terrain/index.html

## Expand description

Terrain analysis algorithms

Algorithms for analyzing Digital Elevation Models (DEMs):

- Slope, Aspect, Hillshade, Curvature, TPI, TRI, Landform
- TWI: Topographic Wetness Index
- SPI/STI: Stream Power / Sediment Transport Index
- Geomorphons: pattern-based landform classification
- Viewshed: line-of-sight visibility analysis
- Sky View Factor, Openness: sky visibility metrics
- Convergence Index: flow convergence/divergence
- Multiscale Curvatures: Florinsky’s robust method
- Feature-Preserving Smoothing: noise removal preserving edges
- Wind Exposure: topographic wind shelter/exposure
- Solar Radiation: beam + diffuse with terrain effects
- MRVBF/MRRTF: multi-resolution valley/ridge flatness
- Northness/Eastness: aspect decomposition
- DEV: Deviation from Mean Elevation
- Multidirectional Hillshade: multi-azimuth shaded relief
- Shape Index & Curvedness: differential geometry measures
- Log Transform: curvature visualization
- Accumulation Zones: flow convergence classification

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use derivatives::`- [Derivatives](https://docs.rs/derivatives/struct.Derivatives.html);
- `pub use derivatives::`- [evans_young](https://docs.rs/derivatives/fn.evans_young.html);
- `pub use derivatives::`- [extract_window](https://docs.rs/derivatives/fn.extract_window.html);
- `pub use derivatives::`- [horn](https://docs.rs/derivatives/fn.horn.html);
- `pub use derivatives::`- [zevenbergen_thorne](https://docs.rs/derivatives/fn.zevenbergen_thorne.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

# surtgis_algorithms::texture - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/texture/index.html

## Expand description

Texture and feature extraction algorithms

- **GLCM**: Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (Haralick textures)
- **LBP**: Local Binary Patterns (Ojala 2002, standard + riu2)
- **Sobel**: Edge detection using Sobel operator
- **Laplacian**: Second-derivative edge enhancement

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Glcm](https://docs.rs/struct.GlcmParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for GLCM computation
- [LbpParams](https://docs.rs/struct.LbpParams.html)
- Parameters for the Local Binary Pattern texture operator.

- [Glcm](https://docs.rs/enum.GlcmTexture.html)- Texture
- Available GLCM texture measures
- [LbpVariant](https://docs.rs/enum.LbpVariant.html)
- LBP variant.

- [haralick_](https://docs.rs/fn.haralick_glcm.html)- glcm
- Compute a single GLCM-based texture feature.
- [haralick_](https://docs.rs/fn.haralick_glcm_multi.html)- glcm_ - multi
- Compute multiple GLCM texture features in a single pass.
- [laplacian](https://docs.rs/fn.laplacian.html)
- Laplacian filter (second-derivative edge detection).
- [lbp](https://docs.rs/fn.lbp.html)
- Compute Local Binary Pattern for each interior pixel of `raster`.
- [sobel_](https://docs.rs/fn.sobel_edge.html)- edge
- Sobel edge detection.

# surtgis_algorithms::vector - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/vector/index.html

## Expand description

Vector analysis algorithms

Geometric operations on vector features:

- Buffer: expand or shrink geometries
- Simplify: reduce vertex count (Douglas-Peucker, Visvalingam)
- Convex hull: minimum enclosing convex polygon
- Centroid: geometric center
- Bounding box: axis-aligned envelope
- Dissolve: merge features by attribute
- Clip: intersect geometries with a boundary
- Area / Length: geometric measurements

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use overlay::`- [difference](https://docs.rs/overlay/fn.difference.html);
- `pub use overlay::`- [dissolve](https://docs.rs/overlay/fn.dissolve.html)as dissolve_overlay;
- `pub use overlay::`- [intersection](https://docs.rs/overlay/fn.intersection.html);
- `pub use overlay::`- [symmetric_difference](https://docs.rs/overlay/fn.symmetric_difference.html);
- `pub use overlay::`- [union](https://docs.rs/overlay/fn.union.html);

- Vector overlay operations: intersection, union, difference, dissolve.

# sha2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sha2/^0.11/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rustcrypto-sha-2)RustCrypto: SHA-2

Pure Rust implementation of the [SHA-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2) cryptographic hash algorithms.

There are 6 standard algorithms specified in the SHA-2 standard:
`Sha224`, `Sha256`, `Sha512_224`, `Sha512_256`, `Sha384`, and `Sha512`.

Algorithmically, there are only 2 core algorithms: SHA-256 and SHA-512. All other algorithms are just applications of these with different initial hash values, and truncated to different digest bit lengths. The first two algorithms in the list are based on SHA-256, while the last four are based on SHA-512.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#one-shot-api)One-shot API

```
use sha2::{Sha256, Digest};
use hex_literal::hex;
let hash = Sha256::digest(b"hello world");
assert_eq!(hash, hex!("b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9"));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#incremental-api)Incremental API

```
use sha2::{Sha256, Sha512, Digest};
use hex_literal::hex;
let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
hasher.update(b"hello ");
hasher.update(b"world");
let hash256 = hasher.finalize();
assert_eq!(hash256, hex!("b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9"));
let mut hasher = Sha512::new();
hasher.update(b"hello world");
let hash512 = hasher.finalize();
assert_eq!(hash512, hex!(
    "309ecc489c12d6eb4cc40f50c902f2b4d0ed77ee511a7c7a9bcd3ca86d4cd86f"
    "989dd35bc5ff499670da34255b45b0cfd830e81f605dcf7dc5542e93ae9cd76f"
));
```
See the [ digest](https://docs.rs/digest) crate docs for additional examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#backends)Backends

This crate supports a number of different backends.

SHA-256 and SHA-512 backends:

- `soft`: portable software implementation
- `loongarch64-asm`:- `asm!`-based implementation for LoongArch64 targets
- `riscv-zknh`: uses the RISC-V- `Zknh`scalar crypto extension. Experimental, requires Nightly compiler and to enable- `Zknh`and- `Zbkb`(or- `Zbb`) target features at compile time.
- `wasm32-simd128`: uses the WASM- `simd128`extension.

SHA-256 only backends:

- `aarch64-sha2`: uses the AArch64- `sha2`extension.
- `x86-sha`: uses the x86 SHA-NI extension.

SHA-512 only backends:

- `aarch64-sha3`: uses the AArch64- `sha3`extension.
- `x86-avx2`: uses the x86 AVX2 extension.

By default the following backends are used:

- `target_arch = "aarch64"`: use- `aarch64-sha2`and- `aarch64-sha3`when the required target features are detected at runtime; otherwise fall back to- `soft`.
- `any(target_arch = "x86", target_arch = "x86_64")`: use- `x86-sha`and- `x86-avx`when the required target features are detected at runtime; otherwise fall back to- `soft`.
- `target_arch = "loongarch64"`: use- `loongarch64-asm`.
- `all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_feature = "simd128")`: use- `wasm32-simd128`.
- All other targets: use `soft`.

You can force backend selection using the following configuration flags:

- `sha2_backend`: select SHA-256 and SHA-512 backends. Supported values:- `soft`,- `riscv-zknh`.
- `sha2_256_backend`: select SHA-256 backend. Supported values:- `aarch64-sha2`,- `soft`,- `riscv-zknh`,- `x86-sha`.
- `sha2_512_backend`: select SHA-512 backend. Supported values:- `aarch64-sha3`,- `soft`,- `riscv-zknh`,- `x86-avx2`.

They can be enabled using either the `RUSTFLAGS` environment variable
(e.g. `RUSTFLAGS='--cfg sha2_backend="soft"'`), or by modifying your `.cargo/config.toml` file.

Note that `sha2_backend` has higher priority than `sha2_256_backend` and `sha2_512_backend`.
In other words, using `--cfg sha2_backend="soft" --cfg sha2_256_backend="x86_sha"` will result
in selection of the software backend for SHA-256.

By default `soft` and `riscv-zknh` backends unroll round loops, which results in a better
performance at the cost of a bigger resulting binary. You can disable unrolling in the backends
by using `sha2_backend_soft = "compact"` and `sha2_backend_riscv_zknh = "compact"` configuration
flags respectively.

at your option.

[276](#276)pub fn job_readiness_packet_payload_hash(packet: &JobReadinessPacket) -> String {
[277](#277)    let evidence_hash = evidence_status_hash(&packet.evidence_status);
[278](#278)    let fuzzy_hash = packet
[279](#279)        .fuzzy_trace
[280](#280)        .as_ref()
[281](#281)        .map_or_else(|| "none".to_string(), fuzzy_trace_hash);
[282](#282)    let forbidden_hash = string_list_hash(&packet.verifier_forbidden_actions);
[283](#283)    let action_hash = string_list_hash(&packet.operator_actions);
[284](#284)    let verdict = packet.verdict.map_or("none", JobVerdict::as_str);
[285](#285)
[286](#286)    sha256_lines(&[
[287](#287)        "job_readiness_packet_payload",
[288](#288)        packet.packet_id.as_str(),
[289](#289)        packet.package_id.as_str(),
[290](#290)        packet.truth_version.as_str(),
[291](#291)        packet.domain_hint.as_str(),
[292](#292)        packet.job_key.as_str(),
[293](#293)        packet.subject_ref.as_str(),
[294](#294)        packet.adapter_receipt_id.as_str(),
[295](#295)        packet.adapter_status.as_str(),
[296](#296)        verdict,
[297](#297)        evidence_hash.as_str(),
[298](#298)        fuzzy_hash.as_str(),
[299](#299)        forbidden_hash.as_str(),
[300](#300)        action_hash.as_str(),
[301](#301)    ])
[302](#302)}

[418](#418)        }
[419](#419)    }
[420](#420)}
[421](#421)
[422](#422)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[423](#423)pub enum OperatorControlError {
[424](#424)    EmptyField {
[425](#425)        field: &'static str,
[426](#426)    },
[427](#427)    EmptyBacklink,
[428](#428)    InvalidBasisPoints {
[429](#429)        field: &'static str,
[430](#430)        value: u16,
[431](#431)    },
[432](#432)    InvalidRange {
[433](#433)        field: &'static str,
[434](#434)        min: u16,
[435](#435)        max: u16,
[436](#436)    },
[437](#437)    InvalidCount {
[438](#438)        field: &'static str,
[439](#439)        value: u32,
[440](#440)    },
[441](#441)    InvalidSha256 {
[442](#442)        field: &'static str,
[443](#443)        value: String,
[444](#444)    },
[445](#445)    DomainActionAuthorityRequested,
[446](#446)}
[447](#447)
[448](#448)impl fmt::Display for OperatorControlError {
[449](#449)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[450](#450)        match self {
[451](#451)            Self::EmptyField { field } => write!(f, "`{field}` must not be empty"),
[452](#452)            Self::EmptyBacklink => write!(f, "backlink ids must not contain empty values"),
[453](#453)            Self::InvalidBasisPoints { field, value } => {
[454](#454)                write!(f, "`{field}` must be between 0 and 10000, got `{value}`")
[455](#455)            }
[456](#456)            Self::InvalidRange { field, min, max } => {
[457](#457)                write!(f, "`{field}` must have min < max, got `{min}`..`{max}`")
[458](#458)            }
[459](#459)            Self::InvalidCount { field, value } => {
[460](#460)                write!(f, "`{field}` must be greater than zero, got `{value}`")
[461](#461)            }
[462](#462)            Self::InvalidSha256 { field, value } => {
[463](#463)                write!(f, "`{field}` must be a sha256 hash, got `{value}`")
[464](#464)            }
[465](#465)            Self::DomainActionAuthorityRequested => {
[466](#466)                write!(f, "job readiness packets must not authorize domain action")
[467](#467)            }
[468](#468)        }
[469](#469)    }
[470](#470)}
[471](#471)
[472](#472)impl Error for OperatorControlError {}
[473](#473)
[474](#474)fn job_readiness_packet_id(input: &JobReadinessPacketInput) -> String {
[475](#475)    let evidence_hash = evidence_status_hash(&input.evidence_status);
[476](#476)    let fuzzy_hash = input
[477](#477)        .fuzzy_trace
[478](#478)        .as_ref()
[479](#479)        .map_or_else(|| "none".to_string(), fuzzy_trace_hash);
[480](#480)    let forbidden_hash = string_list_hash(&input.verifier_forbidden_actions);
[481](#481)    let action_hash = string_list_hash(&input.operator_actions);
[482](#482)    let verdict = input.verdict.map_or("none", JobVerdict::as_str);
[483](#483)
[484](#484)    short_id(
[485](#485)        "helm.job_readiness",
[486](#486)        &sha256_lines(&[
[487](#487)            "job_readiness_packet",
[488](#488)            input.package_id.as_str(),
[489](#489)            input.truth_version.as_str(),
[490](#490)            input.domain_hint.as_str(),
[491](#491)            input.job_key.as_str(),
[492](#492)            input.subject_ref.as_str(),
[493](#493)            input.adapter_receipt_id.as_str(),
[494](#494)            input.adapter_status.as_str(),
[495](#495)            verdict,
[496](#496)            evidence_hash.as_str(),
[497](#497)            fuzzy_hash.as_str(),
[498](#498)            forbidden_hash.as_str(),
[499](#499)            action_hash.as_str(),
[500](#500)        ]),
[501](#501)    )
[502](#502)}
[503](#503)
[504](#504)fn operator_ledger_entry_id(input: &OperatorLedgerEntryInput) -> String {
[505](#505)    let backlinks_hash = string_list_hash(&input.backlink_ids);
[506](#506)    let sequence = input.sequence.to_string();
[507](#507)    short_id(
[508](#508)        "helm.ledger_entry",
[509](#509)        &sha256_lines(&[
[510](#510)            "operator_ledger_entry",
[511](#511)            sequence.as_str(),
[512](#512)            input.record_kind.as_str(),
[513](#513)            input.receipt_family.as_str(),
[514](#514)            input.source_ref.as_str(),
[515](#515)            input.package_id.as_str(),
[516](#516)            input.truth_version.as_str(),
[517](#517)            input.domain_hint.as_str(),
[518](#518)            input.payload_hash.as_str(),
[519](#519)            backlinks_hash.as_str(),
[520](#520)        ]),
[521](#521)    )
[522](#522)}
[523](#523)
[524](#524)fn evidence_status_hash(statuses: &[JobEvidenceStatus]) -> String {
[525](#525)    let mut parts = Vec::new();
[526](#526)    for status in statuses {
[527](#527)        parts.push(status.clause_id.clone());
[528](#528)        parts.push(status.clause_key.clone());
[529](#529)        parts.push(status.label.clone());
[530](#530)        parts.push(status.status.as_str().to_string());
[531](#531)        parts.push(string_list_hash(&status.fact_ids));
[532](#532)        parts.push(string_list_hash(&status.evidence_refs));
[533](#533)        parts.push(string_list_hash(&status.trace_links));
[534](#534)        parts.push(string_list_hash(&status.concern_record_ids));
[535](#535)    }
[536](#536)    string_list_hash(&parts)
[537](#537)}
[538](#538)
[539](#539)fn fuzzy_trace_hash(trace: &FuzzyReadinessTrace) -> String {
[540](#540)    let observed = trace.observed_value_basis_points.to_string();
[541](#541)    let membership_hash = fuzzy_membership_hash(&trace.memberships);
[542](#542)    let rule_hash = fuzzy_rule_hash(&trace.activated_rules);
[543](#543)    let defuzzified_hash = trace
[544](#544)        .defuzzified_score
[545](#545)        .as_ref()
[546](#546)        .map_or_else(|| "none".to_string(), fuzzy_defuzzified_score_hash);
[547](#547)    sha256_lines(&[
[548](#548)        "fuzzy_readiness_trace",
[549](#549)        trace.variable_key.as_str(),
[550](#550)        observed.as_str(),
[551](#551)        membership_hash.as_str(),
[552](#552)        rule_hash.as_str(),
[553](#553)        defuzzified_hash.as_str(),
[554](#554)    ])
[555](#555)}
[556](#556)
[557](#557)fn fuzzy_membership_hash(memberships: &[FuzzyMembership]) -> String {
[558](#558)    let mut parts = Vec::new();
[559](#559)    for membership in memberships {
[560](#560)        parts.push(membership.label.clone());
[561](#561)        parts.push(membership.score_basis_points.to_string());
[562](#562)    }
[563](#563)    string_list_hash(&parts)
[564](#564)}
[565](#565)
[566](#566)fn fuzzy_rule_hash(rules: &[FuzzyRuleActivation]) -> String {
[567](#567)    let mut parts = Vec::new();
[568](#568)    for rule in rules {
[569](#569)        parts.push(rule.rule_id.clone());
[570](#570)        parts.push(rule.strength_basis_points.to_string());
[571](#571)        parts.push(rule.conclusion.clone());
[572](#572)    }
[573](#573)    string_list_hash(&parts)
[574](#574)}
[575](#575)
[576](#576)fn fuzzy_defuzzified_score_hash(score: &FuzzyDefuzzifiedScore) -> String {
[577](#577)    let score_basis_points = score.score_basis_points.to_string();
[578](#578)    let domain_min_basis_points = score.domain_min_basis_points.to_string();
[579](#579)    let domain_max_basis_points = score.domain_max_basis_points.to_string();
[580](#580)    let domain_steps = score.domain_steps.to_string();
[581](#581)    sha256_lines(&[
[582](#582)        "fuzzy_defuzzified_score",
[583](#583)        score.method.as_str(),
[584](#584)        score_basis_points.as_str(),
[585](#585)        domain_min_basis_points.as_str(),
[586](#586)        domain_max_basis_points.as_str(),
[587](#587)        domain_steps.as_str(),
[588](#588)    ])
[589](#589)}
[590](#590)
[591](#591)fn string_list_hash(values: &[String]) -> String {
[592](#592)    let refs = values.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>();
[593](#593)    sha256_lines(&refs)
[594](#594)}
[595](#595)
[596](#596)fn validate_fuzzy_trace(trace: &FuzzyReadinessTrace) -> Result<(), OperatorControlError> {
[597](#597)    validate_nonempty("fuzzy_trace.variable_key", &trace.variable_key)?;
[598](#598)    validate_basis_points(
[599](#599)        "fuzzy_trace.observed_value_basis_points",
[600](#600)        trace.observed_value_basis_points,
[601](#601)    )?;
[602](#602)    if trace.memberships.is_empty() {
[603](#603)        return Err(OperatorControlError::EmptyField {
[604](#604)            field: "fuzzy_trace.memberships",
[605](#605)        });
[606](#606)    }
[607](#607)    for membership in &trace.memberships {
[608](#608)        validate_nonempty("fuzzy_trace.membership.label", &membership.label)?;
[609](#609)        validate_basis_points(
[610](#610)            "fuzzy_trace.membership.score_basis_points",
[611](#611)            membership.score_basis_points,
[612](#612)        )?;
[613](#613)    }
[614](#614)    for rule in &trace.activated_rules {
[615](#615)        validate_nonempty("fuzzy_trace.rule.rule_id", &rule.rule_id)?;
[616](#616)        validate_basis_points(
[617](#617)            "fuzzy_trace.rule.strength_basis_points",
[618](#618)            rule.strength_basis_points,
[619](#619)        )?;
[620](#620)        validate_nonempty("fuzzy_trace.rule.conclusion", &rule.conclusion)?;
[621](#621)    }
[622](#622)    if let Some(score) = &trace.defuzzified_score {
[623](#623)        validate_nonempty("fuzzy_trace.defuzzified_score.method", &score.method)?;
[624](#624)        validate_basis_points(
[625](#625)            "fuzzy_trace.defuzzified_score.score_basis_points",
[626](#626)            score.score_basis_points,
[627](#627)        )?;
[628](#628)        validate_basis_points(
[629](#629)            "fuzzy_trace.defuzzified_score.domain_min_basis_points",
[630](#630)            score.domain_min_basis_points,
[631](#631)        )?;
[632](#632)        validate_basis_points(
[633](#633)            "fuzzy_trace.defuzzified_score.domain_max_basis_points",
[634](#634)            score.domain_max_basis_points,
[635](#635)        )?;
[636](#636)        if score.domain_min_basis_points >= score.domain_max_basis_points {
[637](#637)            return Err(OperatorControlError::InvalidRange {
[638](#638)                field: "fuzzy_trace.defuzzified_score.domain",
[639](#639)                min: score.domain_min_basis_points,
[640](#640)                max: score.domain_max_basis_points,
[641](#641)            });
[642](#642)        }
[643](#643)        if score.domain_steps == 0 {
[644](#644)            return Err(OperatorControlError::InvalidCount {
[645](#645)                field: "fuzzy_trace.defuzzified_score.domain_steps",
[646](#646)                value: score.domain_steps,
[647](#647)            });
[648](#648)        }
[649](#649)    }
[650](#650)    Ok(())
[651](#651)}
[652](#652)
[653](#653)fn validate_basis_points(field: &'static str, value: u16) -> Result<(), OperatorControlError> {
[654](#654)    if value <= 10_000 {
[655](#655)        Ok(())
[656](#656)    } else {
[657](#657)        Err(OperatorControlError::InvalidBasisPoints { field, value })
[658](#658)    }
[659](#659)}
[660](#660)
[661](#661)fn validate_nonempty(field: &'static str, value: &str) -> Result<(), OperatorControlError> {
[662](#662)    if value.trim().is_empty() {
[663](#663)        Err(OperatorControlError::EmptyField { field })
[664](#664)    } else {
[665](#665)        Ok(())
[666](#666)    }
[667](#667)}
[668](#668)
[669](#669)fn validate_sha256(field: &'static str, value: &str) -> Result<(), OperatorControlError> {
[670](#670)    if value.strip_prefix("sha256:").is_some_and(|digest| {
[671](#671)        digest.len() == 64 && digest.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit())
[672](#672)    }) {
[673](#673)        Ok(())
[674](#674)    } else {
[675](#675)        Err(OperatorControlError::InvalidSha256 {
[676](#676)            field,
[677](#677)            value: value.to_string(),
[678](#678)        })
[679](#679)    }
[680](#680)}
[681](#681)
[682](#682)fn short_id(prefix: &str, digest: &str) -> String {
[683](#683)    let short_digest = &digest
[684](#684)        .strip_prefix("sha256:")
[685](#685)        .expect("local digest has sha256 prefix")[..12];
[686](#686)    format!("{prefix}.{short_digest}")
[687](#687)}
[688](#688)
[689](#689)fn sha256_lines(parts: &[&str]) -> String {
[690](#690)    sha256_bytes(parts.join("\n").as_bytes())
[691](#691)}
[692](#692)
[693](#693)fn sha256_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
[694](#694)    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
[695](#695)    hasher.update(bytes);
[696](#696)    let digest = hasher.finalize();
[697](#697)    let mut output = String::with_capacity("sha256:".len() + digest.len() * 2);
[698](#698)    output.push_str("sha256:");
[699](#699)    for byte in digest {
[700](#700)        write!(&mut output, "{byte:02x}").expect("writing to String cannot fail");
[701](#701)    }
[702](#702)    output
[703](#703)}
[704](#704)

[895](#895)    fn sample_packet_input() -> JobReadinessPacketInput {
[896](#896)        JobReadinessPacketInput {

    pub verifier_forbidden_actions: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub operator_actions: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
}## Expand description

Helm-owned read model for “can this job be trusted enough for an operator to continue reviewing it?”

This is intentionally not an Axiom type. Axiom supplies packages, reports, clause ids, and adapter receipts. Helm composes those with app subject refs, missing-evidence actions, and operator ledger links.

```
pub struct OperatorLedgerEntry {
    pub entry_id:

    pub summary: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
}## Expand description

Deterministic append-only ledger entry for Helm operator-control receipts.

This is a control-plane journal entry. It stores ids, refs, hashes, and backlinks; it does not store raw app transcripts and it never grants domain authority.
